answer.evidence: The top cap (rows 1-6) is light with a blue inset stripe at rows 3-4. The width profile 10, 12, 12, then 14 shows chamfered back corners. The cap ends in a grey front-edge line at row 6, then a dark outline at row 7 and a darker shadow row at row 8. This fits evidence (a). Below it is a tall dark-blue sign face with white lettering (rows 8-27) and a dark base (rows 28-30), which gives about 22 rows of front face. This is a borderline call. The cap could instead be read as a face-on header plate, in which case the object would be front_elevation. I judged it a top surface because of the edge line, the shadow and the narrowed back corners.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign: a pale blue-white panel with a dark navy border and Korean glyphs. It measures 8 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0% and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the navy outline is tinted and reads as dark material tone, not a sticker line. The panel has only about 3 lightness steps (white-blue face, mid blue, dark navy) with a small cap highlight. It lacks the grain, per-part shading and detail of kiosk-a and vending-a. On the primary facts it sits in the middle of the references, but by eye it is flatter than the two richer ones, though comparable to the simple bus shelter. A sign is a thin, simple object, so it should not fail for sparseness alone. It is clean and consistent with the chipset, and a careful artist would accept it next to the bus shelter.

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall, flat, vertical panel. Rows 8-27 hold the blue face with white lettering, and rows 28-30 are a dark base. The header at rows 1-6 is a light frame with a blue stripe at rows 3-4. It reads as a face-on header plate, not a horizontal surface. It has no ellipse and no clear front-edge line with an eave shadow. Row 6 is gray and row 7 is the dark outline, which only makes a rim-like 1-2 row hint. The width profile (10, 12, then 14 from row 3 to row 30) only shows rounded upper corners, not a widening and narrowing cap. No contents or roof are visible and no side face is drawn. The whole object reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign: a dark navy body with a light-blue panel and white Korean glyphs (편의). It has 8 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outline is tinted navy rather than black. Measured facts are above bus-shelter-a (6 tones) but below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). By eye the body is shaded in only about 3 steps (dark outline, mid navy, light panel), with little grain or highlight work on the frame. The vending machine and kiosk carry more distinct highlight bands, trim details and per-part shading. The candidate is simple and cleanly drawn, but it looks flatter than the better references. The tinted outline and the lack of flat fills keep it from being a sticker look, yet it is not clearly at the level of kiosk-a or vending-a. When in doubt, fail.

answer.evidence: The sign is a flat vertical board drawn face-on. The width profile goes 10, 12, then 14 for rows 3-30. That is a small bevel at the corners, not an ellipse. Rows 1-6 form a light header with a blue stripe. It reads as a vertical label plate: the stripe is a face-on detail, there is no front-edge line followed by eave shadow, and row 7 is just the dark outline. The main body (rows 8-27) is a blue panel with white lettering and has no horizontal surface. Rows 28-30 are a dark base strip, also face-on. No top surface is shown and no receding side face is drawn, so it matches the red 'front elevation' references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical sign panel with a dark navy-tinted outline, a light face with a shaded edge and dark Korean lettering. Measured facts: 8 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for the bus shelter. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted like the references and not a black sticker line. The panel has about 4 lightness steps, a little shallower than the references' 5, and little grain beyond the lettering and rim shading. As a thin single-panel prop it is not thinner or flatter than the accepted bus-shelter, so it holds up beside the references. It is a modest pass, not a rich one.

answer.evidence: Rows 1-6 form a light top band, with a white highlight at row 1, a blue inset at rows 3-4, and a gray lower edge at row 6. A dark line at row 7 closes the band, and row 8 is a darker blue strip that works as eave shadow. The silhouette narrows from 12 to 10 px at the top rows, so the corners read as rounded. Below the cap, the blue face runs through rows 8-27 and a dark base through rows 28-30, which gives about 23 rows of front face. The cap could also be read as a face-on header panel, so this call is borderline. I counted it as a top surface because it has a front-edge line and a shadow row below it.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical standing sign: a blue-white body with a dark blue frame and a Korean text panel. It measures 8 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted dark blue and not black. That is above bus-shelter-a (6 tones, 9% flat) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). The sign face has a highlight edge, a mid body, a shadow side and the lettering, which gives about 4 steps against 5-6 on the references. Texture is limited to the lettering and a few edge highlights, with no grain, but there are no large flat areas. It sits at the lower end of the accepted range for a thin, simple signboard and would look acceptable beside bus-shelter-a, though somewhat thinner than kiosk-a and vending-a.
